items.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: Joe Williams did that, Betty Carter used to sing it I hear.

ctx.x: Yes, she was. She is a marvelous singer. And my father was [Mark] Moose Charlap who was a songwriter/composer. The most famous thing he’s known for is the music from “Peter Pan,” — Mary Martin Peter Pan, which he wrote most of the music for — songs

like “I’m Flying,” “I’ve Gotta Crow,” “Tender Shepherd,” “I Won’t Grow Up,” that’s all my dad, as many pop songs such as “I Was Telling Her About You,” you might know that one, Joe Williams did that, Betty Carter used to sing it I hear. And many others. He died when I was quite young, I was six or seven years old. And he was only in his 40s, so he would have gone on. But my parents are both related very closely, they lived in the tradition of the American popular song, and that is a very focal point for me, it’s…
So you were surrounded by that in your house as you grew up, that music.
